extracted.intended_audience: Prospective NIA grant applicants (especially F99/K00, K99/R00, and early-career researchers preparing sample application materials)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for how to use National Institute on Aging (NIA) sample applications and summary statements as examples when preparing fellowship, career-development, and related grant submissions. Emphasizes limits of the samples and procedural cautions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Samples_are_examples_not_templates
rubrics_metrics.description: These are only examples of successful applications and are not meant to be a template for future applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make sure that your application is tailored to your specific research and career development plan and seek individual advice from mentors and peers as you prepare your application. Do not copy the samples verbatim; use them to learn about organization, level of detail, and presentation rather than as a fill-in template.

rubrics_metrics.name: Always_follow_your_funding_opportunity_instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Always follow your funding opportunity's instructions for application format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although these applications demonstrate good grantsmanship, time has passed since these grantees applied. The samples may not reflect the latest format or rules. Use the official FOA and current application forms as the authoritative source for formatting, page limits, required attachments, and submission procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailor_to_specific_research_and_career_plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Please make sure that your application is tailored to your specific research and career development plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content and emphasis should reflect the applicant's unique project aims, training needs, and career trajectory; examples from others should be adapted rather than adopted wholesale. Seek individualized feedback from mentors and peers to ensure alignment with your goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review_initial_and_resubmission_examples_plus_summary_statements
rubrics_metrics.description: The F99/K00 and K99/R00 resources below represent the initial submissions and subsequent resubmissions of applications from applicants who received an excellent score and were funded upon resubmission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare the unfunded initial applications, the reviewers' summary statements, and the funded resubmissions to understand how applications were revised in response to reviewer critiques. Use summary statements to learn common reviewer concerns and how resubmissions addressed them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Samples_may_be_outdated
rubrics_metrics.description: Although these applications demonstrate good grantsmanship, time has passed since these grantees applied. The samples may not reflect the latest format or rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume sample structure, forms version, or required attachments are current. Verify current requirements on the relevant FOA and NIH/NIA submission pages before preparing or submitting your application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright_and_permitted_use
rubrics_metrics.description: The awardee allows you to use the material (e.g., data, writing, graphics) it shared in this application only for nonprofit educational purposes provided the material remains unchanged and the principal investigator, awardee organization, and NIH NIA are credited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you reuse excerpts from the sample applications for teaching or training, keep the material unchanged and include the required credit lines. Do not republish or adapt the content for purposes outside nonprofit education without additional permission.
